decision: Build one new pure module src/core/dual-control.ts (zero IO, zero migration, zero new authority store) owning: (1) dualControlDecision(input) -> {required_approvers:1|2, distinct_ok, satisfied, reason} keyed to criticality where required_approvers===2 iff criticalityDiff(from,to).escalates===true OR the Q-2 implicit-escalate fires; (2) nonDerivableReadClearance(addedReadGrants) the Q-2 fail-closed detector reusing frozen isDataClass; (3) buildConfirmationFlag(...) assembling the DERIVED in-request {change_ref, effective_diff, approvers[], status} record (Q-1, no persistence); (4) encodeDualControlAuditEvent(...) a thin pure encoder producing a dualcontrol.gate AuditEventInput (T-0031 contract). The integration seam edits src/http/grants.ts: at POST /api/grants and POST /api/role-assignments, after validateAdminDelegation and BEFORE the INSERT, fold the role's effective grants before/after the proposed change via combineCriticality, compute criticalityDiff, call dualControlDecision with approvers[] from the request body, reject unsatisfied changes with HTTP 4xx DUAL_CONTROL_UNSATISFIED (no confirmed row written), and on success append the dualcontrol.gate WORM event via the CANONICAL appendAuditEventInput in the same transaction as the INSERT + the existing grant/assignment audit event. confirmation_flag is DERIVED-not-stored: no table, no migration, known_tenant_tables.txt byte-unchanged (T-0040 §6-B precedent). Q-3: enforcement attaches at the existing single-INSERT write-path with approvers[] in one request; the durable multi-request half-confirmed workflow is the downstream human-approval task (out of scope, would own migration 031). Q-2: a newly-added read grant whose clearance marker is present-but-non-derivable is an implicit escalate (fail-closed, NF-2), closing the T-0040 R-1 under-flag without editing frozen T-0040/T-0033. A new fitness gate ci/checks/dual-control-isolation.sh (no-IO, no-Date.now, single-source-of-criticality, no-SoD, no-parallel-authority, frozen-foundation, no-migration, known_tenant_tables-unchanged) is appended to npm run fitness. Orchestrator ruling (founder-autonomy-impl frame): D-A=A3 direction signed; Q-1/Q-2/Q-3 implementation shape applied as a given, recorded in friction ledger FE-2026-W24-0044. REV-2 (BINDING, ADR §9): the rev-1 §Q-3 mechanism of carrying BOTH approver identities in one request body (approvers: string[]) authenticated by a single x-dev-user actor is WITHDRAWN as decorative dual-control (one principal could name any second approver — same body-asserted-authority hole T-0030 closed for isGenesisOwner; inverts D-A=A3). R-AUTH: every approver's identity is taken ONLY from the authenticated context (extractActor) of THAT approver's own request; the body MUST NOT carry approvers[]/confirmed_by/confirmed2_by for an escalating change. A single HTTP request has exactly one authenticated actor, so an authentic two-approver gate is STRUCTURALLY a two-request flow: confirm-request #1 lands the escalating row SEMI-CONFIRMED (confirmed_by=extractActor(req1), confirmed2_by NULL — NOT active); a separate authenticated confirm-request #2 sets confirmed2_by=extractActor(req2) only if actor2 != proposed_by AND actor2 != confirmed_by (distinctness over authenticated ids, read from the DB row not the body), transitioning semi-confirmed->confirmed and writing a second dual-control.second-confirm WORM event. The pure dualControlDecision core is unchanged; the call-site provenance + two-request shape change. Day-1 activation = contract + write-gard (no runtime read-filter exists yet: role->grants EFFECTIVE resolution is T-0053; obligation FE-2026-W24-0044-B requires T-0053 to filter confirmed2_by-NULL escalating grants as not-active). DDL is now NECESSARY (rev-1's ddl_needed:none was an artifact of faking both approvers in one body): migration 031 adds one additive nullable column confirmed2_by to choros."grant" and choros.role_assignment (mirrors migration 030; no new table, no RLS change, known_tenant_tables.txt byte-unchanged) — Q-1-compliant (status column OK; new flag TABLE forbidden). New fitness FF-DC11 bans body-sourced approver identity. Rev-2 also closes the pre-existing confirmed_by=b[confirmed_by] body-assertion on the routine path (confirmed_by now = extractActor(req), proposer cannot self-confirm).

rejected_alternatives.option: Persist confirmation_flag as a new tenant_id-bearing table (+ migration 031, RLS, known_tenant_tables.txt churn, cross-tenant fitness case)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Q-1 ruling: day-1 minimum is a DERIVED decision + WORM audit. A table duplicates state reconstructable from audit_event + grant rows, adds a tenant-isolation surface and migration cost the spec §6 explicitly parks for the downstream approval-workflow task. T-0040 §6-B derived-not-stored precedent.

rejected_alternatives.option: Re-derive the three axis bits inside the gate (skip T-0040)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Splits the source of truth (FR-8, AC-13). Gate and computation could drift silently — the exact anti-pattern T-0040 froze the seam to prevent. The gate consumes criticalityDiff/combineCriticality, never re-derives.

rejected_alternatives.option: Inherit T-0040's R-1 under-flag (garbage clearance => no escalation)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Q-2 ruling rejects the permissive direction: it leaves garbage-clearance privilege expansions completing with one approver — the precise preventive-brake case D-A=A3 was chosen to close. Fail-closed (NF-2): a non-derivable clearance on an added read grant is an implicit escalate.

rejected_alternatives.option: Edit role-criticality.ts/data-classification.ts to over-flag axis c on corrupt clearance
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Frozen foundation (NF-5). The fix lives on T-0044's side as a detector over the change's added read grants reusing the frozen isDataClass; the frozen modules stay byte-untouched.

rejected_alternatives.option: Introduce a two-phase propose->confirm endpoint pair + durable half-confirmed state (migration 031)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Q-3 ruling: the multi-request human-approval workflow is a DOWNSTREAM consumer (spec §5/§6). Day-1 attaches the gate at the existing single-INSERT write-path with approvers[] in one request — exercised end-to-end by a real consumer (D-056 integration-honesty) with zero DDL. The durable workflow task, if ever built, owns migration 031.

rejected_alternatives.option: Add a new audit writer / parallel audit path for dualcontrol.gate
rejected_alternatives.why_not: NF-7: emission MUST use the existing T-0031 AuditEventInput encoder contract + the canonical appendAuditEventInput in the same transaction. T-0044 adds only a thin pure AuditEventInput encoder, not a second append path.

rejected_alternatives.option: Have the gate call the T-0032 SoD evaluator to reuse the distinctness check
rejected_alternatives.why_not: AC-18: dual-control and SoD are independent gates. SoD answers role-incompatibility-for-one-principal; dual-control answers did-a-criticality-expansion-get-two-distinct-approvers. Coupling conflates two orthogonal controls.

rejected_alternatives.option: [REV-2 WITHDRAWN — was rev-1 §Q-3] Carry both approver identities in one request body (approvers: string[]) authenticated by a single x-dev-user actor; one-request single-INSERT guard
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Decorative dual-control: one authenticated principal could name ANY second approver in the body and satisfy a 2-approver gate alone — the same body-asserted-authority hole T-0030 closed by sourcing isGenesisOwner from the DB not the body, and identical to today's confirmed_by=b[confirmed_by]. It INVERTS D-A=A3 (the preventive brake becomes a rubber stamp). Rev-2 R-AUTH: every approver identity comes ONLY from the authenticated context (extractActor) of that approver's own request; since one request has exactly one authenticated actor, the gate is structurally a two-request flow (ADR §9).

rejected_alternatives.option: [REV-2] Keep ddl_needed:none by persisting approver2 only in the WORM audit payload (no confirmed2_by column)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The second-confirm write-gard must enforce distinctness (actor2 != proposed_by AND != confirmed_by) by reading the target row's confirmed-by state, and any future EFFECTIVE resolver must distinguish semi-confirmed (confirmed2_by NULL) from confirmed as queryable ROW state — an append-only audit event is not row-state. A durable nullable column confirmed2_by (migration 031, additive, mirrors 030) is the honest minimum and is Q-1-compliant (status column, not a new flag table).

contracts: export function buildConfirmationFlag(args: {changeRef: string; diff: CriticalityDiff; approvers: string[]; status: ConfirmationFlagStatus}): ConfirmationFlag

export function encodeDualControlAuditEvent(args: {flag: ConfirmationFlag; decision: DualControlDecision; changeKind: 'grant'|'assignment'; actor: string; proposedBy: string; primaryConfirmer: string | null; nowMs: number}): AuditEventInput
import { criticalityDiff, combineCriticality, type RoleCriticality, type CriticalityDiff } from './role-criticality.js' (single source of truth, FR-8)
import { type Grant, isEffective } from './grant-lattice.js'; import { isDataClass } from './data-classification.js' (Q-2 probe only, read-only)
Distinctness invariant: D = unique(approvers) \ {proposedBy}; required 2 => satisfied iff |D|>=2; required 1 => satisfied iff |D|>=1; flag.approvers = D

Integration (grants.ts, both write-paths): after validateAdminDelegation, before INSERT, inside withTenantTx — fold from/to via combineCriticality, call dualControlDecision; if !satisfied throw HttpError(4xx, 'DUAL_CONTROL_UNSATISFIED', reason) and write no confirmed row; on success append dualcontrol.gate via appendAuditEventInput in the same tx (confirmed_by=approver1)

[REV-2 — SUPERSEDES the body-asserted approvers[] integration above] R-AUTH write-gard (ADR §9.6): every approver id = extractActor(req) of its OWN request, never a body field. CONFIRM-REQUEST #1: actor=extractActor(req); dualControlDecision called with proposedBy=actor, approvers=[]; if required_approvers===1 (routine) and actor!==proposedBy -> INSERT confirmed_by=actor, confirmed2_by=NULL (active); if required_approvers===2 -> INSERT proposed_by=actor, confirmed_by=actor, confirmed2_by=NULL (SEMI-CONFIRMED, NOT active), append dualcontrol.gate(status:pending). CONFIRM-REQUEST #2 (phase=confirm2 on change_ref, same endpoints): actor2=extractActor(req); SELECT proposed_by/confirmed_by/confirmed2_by FROM target (DB, not body); reject if confirmed2_by NOT NULL (already_confirmed) or actor2===proposed_by or actor2===confirmed_by (self_confirm, 409 DUAL_CONTROL_UNSATISFIED); else UPDATE confirmed2_by=actor2 WHERE confirmed2_by IS NULL, append dualcontrol.gate(via:'dual-control.second-confirm', confirmed_by:actor2, status:satisfied). The distinct approver set into buildConfirmationFlag/encodeDualControlAuditEvent = {confirmed_by(req1), confirmed2_by(req2)}, both authenticated.

[REV-2] Body MUST NOT carry approvers[] / confirmed_by / confirmed2_by for an escalating change; such fields are ignored. FF-DC11 bans the gate call-site from reading approver identity out of the body (no b["approvers"]/b["confirmed2_by"] feeding the gate/INSERT on the dual-control path). Routine path also moves confirmed_by from b["confirmed_by"] to extractActor(req) (closes pre-existing grants.ts:470 body-assertion).

[REV-2] migration 031 (additive): ALTER TABLE choros."grant" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS confirmed2_by text NULL; same on choros.role_assignment. Mirrors migration 030 — no new table, no RLS change, known_tenant_tables.txt byte-unchanged, idempotent.
